content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate cupcake without icing is a small, moist piece of cake infused with cocoa, without any additional topping. It delivers a rich chocolate flavor, a tender crumb, and a slightly wet texture, making it an ideal treat for pure chocolate lovers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cupcakes without icing are often served in cafés as a quick snack or coffee accompaniment.
Traditional chocolate cupcakes are made from flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and cocoa powder.
Skipping the icing reduces sugar and calorie content compared to frosted versions.
Cocoa used in the cupcake is rich in antioxidants that may support heart health.
In some regions these are called "plain" or "naked" chocolate cupcakes.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals and support vascular function.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa contributes to muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Chocolate cupcakes can aid in maintaining normal hemoglobin levels thanks to a modest iron content.

items.title: Provides some fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the cupcake adds dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates and a small amount of fat offers a quick and sustained source of energy.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Standard recipes use wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without icing, sugar is still present; those monitoring blood glucose should watch portion size.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of caffeine, which may affect sleep in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The cupcake remains calorie‑dense due to butter and sugar; moderation is key for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cupcake on its own, split it and top with fresh berries, ice cream, or yogurt. It also travels well in a lunchbox as a quick snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cupcake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 2 months). Let it come to room temperature before serving.
